question: A fish stock grows by breeding. Below, its size as a share of the unfished sea. When does it add the most fish?
answer: At half full; a full sea adds almost none. Food and space run short, so births barely replace deaths. In Schaefer's 1954 model, growth peaks at half the unfished stock: plenty of parents, room to spare. That is the logic of maximum sustainable yield: a half-empty sea feeds the most boats.
move: Expect growth to peak halfway up, not at the full.
ask: What in my life is so full that it has stopped growing?

scene.label: New fish a year, % of the peak

verdict.under: Right at the floor: a full sea adds almost nothing. The peak comes at half full.
verdict.near: Right: a sea at its natural limit adds almost nothing. Growth peaks at half full.
verdict.over: Fewer: a full sea adds almost no fish a year. Growth peaks at half full.

reference: Schaefer, Some aspects of the dynamics of populations important to the management of the commercial marine fisheries, Bulletin of the Inter-American Tropical Tuna Commission 1(2):27-56, 1954 (yearly growth proportional to N(1 - N/K))
